analysis: Two files changed. (1) docs/reference/qwen4-next-support.md: the date bump and a new sentence (head lines 79-82) say every concrete Qwen3.8-27B build in ModelRuntimeRequirements.qwen38ConcreteModelIDs shares the reasoning-effort rejection boundary. This is documentation only. It changes no controls and makes no security claim that contradicts the threat model. I could not verify the cited symbol or the underlying Qwen4SupportPolicy.validateReasoningContext extension, because those sources were not supplied. (2) MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift: the patch adds one line at head line 734 in a catch block. It rethrows MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError as-is, ahead of the EngineV2VisionPrefillError mapping. Only the hunk was supplied, not the surrounding head text. The visible base text ends at line 530, before the changed region. From the patch alone, this appears to preserve typed engine errors, such as invalidToolPayload, through the vision/media preparation path instead of letting them fall to a generic mapping. The security-relevant question is whether those errors can carry sensitive content, such as prompt or tool-schema text, to the consumer or coordinator. Typed errors flow through ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift (sanitizedInferenceFailure), which is not supplied. Relevant threat IDs are T-008 and A-001, only as a data-exposure concern. No concrete regression is established. A later pass should confirm that MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError messages are bounded and sanitized, and that the early rethrow does not skip releaseBox.fire() or the reservation cleanup the catch block performs. The hunk context does not show whether cleanup happens before this rethrow or at the outer level. I flagged needs_deeper_review for that reason.
